contracts.commit_point: A database mutation would commit at client.execute / client.execute_many inside a subagent-dispatched write tool (shared/tools/postgres.py:472 and 571); the guard's enforcement point is the explorer toolset assembly passed to create_agent (agents/supervisor/nodes/supervisor.py:107-111).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Name-based read-only allowlist in _get_explorer_tools: read_only_tools = [t for t in tools if t.name in ('postgres_query', 'postgres_get_schema')]; only the filtered list is passed as the tools argument to create_agent for the explorer subgraph.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Binding postgres_execute or postgres_execute_batch into the database explorer subagent's tool set: PostgresClient.get_tools() returns all four tools including the two write tools, and _get_explorer_tools must remove every tool whose name is not postgres_query or postgres_get_schema.
pending_binding_information: Whether any construction path other than _get_explorer_tools can create the explorer subgraph with an unfiltered tool list (only this path appears in the supplied views).
contracts.protected_operation: Construction and tool dispatch of the database explorer subagent created by _create_database_explorer_subgraph (create_agent with the filtered explorer tool list), which is itself invoked as the supervisor tool database_explorer_subagent.
contracts.protected_resource: The PostgreSQL database reachable through the shared PostgresClient connection pool (the same data and schema that the excluded write tools would mutate).
contracts.protection_obligation: The database explorer subagent must be provisioned only with read-only PostgreSQL tools (postgres_query, postgres_get_schema); the write tools (postgres_execute, postgres_execute_batch) must be filtered out before the explorer subgraph is constructed, so no database write can be dispatched through the explorer.
scope_limits: The read-only restriction applies only to the explorer subagent; the supervisor agent itself receives the full unfiltered tool set including postgres_execute and postgres_execute_batch (agents/supervisor/nodes/supervisor.py:214-220).
The filter is name-membership based at subagent construction time; it does not re-validate tool identity at dispatch time.
This guard constrains only which tools are bound to the explorer; it adds no approval step to any write executed through other paths.

contracts.commit_point: await client.execute(statement, *params) inside postgres_execute (shared/tools/postgres.py:472) and await client.execute_many(statement, args_list) inside postgres_execute_batch (shared/tools/postgres.py:571), each reached only after the approval check passes.
contracts.declared_mechanism: In-tool approval gate: when config.postgres_write_requires_approval is True, the tool calls _request_write_approval, which formats the statement (plus a batch summary for bulk operations) and calls langgraph.types.interrupt() to suspend for a human response; _is_write_approved validates the reply; a non-approval returns 'Operation cancelled: User rejected the write operation...' before execution; GraphInterrupt is re-raised for LangGraph human-in-the-loop handling. The flag postgres_write_requires_approval is declared in SeerConfig with default True.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Executing a write SQL statement through postgres_execute (leading to PostgresClient.execute) or postgres_execute_batch (leading to PostgresClient.execute_many) when config.postgres_write_requires_approval is True and the interrupt response is absent, None, or not in the approval token set ('yes', 'y', 'approve', 'approved', 'ok', 'proceed', 'true', '1').
pending_binding_information: The deployment-time value of postgres_write_requires_approval (env/.env contents not supplied; only the Pydantic default of True is supported by the source).

Which serving layer/checkpointer surfaces the interrupt to a human and resumes the graph: config describes database_uri as required for human-in-the-loop interrupts (shared/config.py:93-96) and the supervisor node re-raises GraphInterrupt (agents/supervisor/nodes/supervisor.py:353-357), but the graph assembly/checkpointer wiring is not in the supplied views.
Whether postgres_execute/postgres_execute_batch are bound to any agents or entry points other than the supervisor agent (repository enumeration is not complete).
contracts.protected_operation: Agent-invoked write tool calls: postgres_execute(statement, parameters) and postgres_execute_batch(statement, parameters_list) defined inside _create_tools_for_client.
contracts.protected_resource: The PostgreSQL database reachable through the PostgresClient connection pool (data and schema mutated by client.execute / client.execute_many on the configured connection string).
contracts.protection_obligation: PostgreSQL write statements (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DDL) invoked through the agent tools postgres_execute and postgres_execute_batch must obtain explicit human approval via a LangGraph interrupt, gated by config.postgres_write_requires_approval (default True), before any execution; if the human response is not an approval token, the write is cancelled and never reaches the database client. (Merged from both first- and second-phase reviewer opinions, which describe the same obligation.)
scope_limits: The gate is conditional on config.postgres_write_requires_approval; the flag is loaded from environment/.env via Pydantic Settings, so a deployment setting it to False disables approval entirely and writes execute without any interrupt.

The approval gate exists only inside the postgres_execute/postgres_execute_batch tool wrappers; PostgresClient.execute and client.execute_many themselves are ungated, so non-tool callers (e.g., PostgresProvider.provision_resources/cleanup_resources at shared/tools/postgres.py:742 and 772) would bypass approval.

postgres_query's read-only enforcement is a separate SELECT/WITH prefix check routed through client.query (conn.fetch); it sits outside this approval gate, so a WITH-prefixed statement containing data modification would not traverse the gate.
Approval is a simple string match on the interrupt response and presumes a LangGraph runtime in which interrupt() suspends and resumes with a human reply (the tools re-raise GraphInterrupt).

missing_information: Deployment/runtime value of postgres_write_requires_approval: supplied source shows only the Pydantic default True (shared/config.py:102-105); environment/.env overrides are not visible.

Graph assembly and checkpointer wiring that surfaces the LangGraph interrupt to a human and resumes the supervisor graph: config notes database_uri is required for human-in-the-loop interrupts (shared/config.py:93-96) and the supervisor node re-raises GraphInterrupt, but the serving/checkpointer wiring is outside the supplied views.
Complete set of call sites binding postgres_execute/postgres_execute_batch or PostgresClient tools to agents or entry points (repository enumeration is not complete).

Whether statements routed through postgres_query (e.g., WITH-prefixed data-modifying CTEs that would pass the SELECT/WITH prefix check and execute via client.query/conn.fetch) are intended to be covered by the write-approval requirement; the supplied source does not establish this intent.
